note: Narration is first person in the author's own cloned voice; 'stevan' and 'ana' lines are the call, as the CI film's script says them. Every claim is checked against the footage named in BRIEF.md.

lines.text: And what was our trial-to-paid conversion last month, by the way?
Someone asks for a number on a call. LokalBot saw it on my screen last week, and answers before I've found the tab.
LokalBot already records my meetings and remembers my screen, on my Mac. For this hackathon, I connected that memory to three Meta models.
I'm on a call with Ana about our launch. I press Start Radar, and a small panel floats over the call.
Hi! Okay, launch checklist. The pricing page is almost done, I just need the final numbers.
I'll send the revised pricing deck to Marko by Friday.
Muse Voice Transcribe turns each turn into text as it ends. Muse Spark reads it, and my commitment lands seconds later.
Great. What did we put as the Team plan price in the pricing sheet?
One second, it's in the sheet.
Muse Wonder looks it up in my work. It starts from what LokalBot remembers, then searches my documents and opens the sheet.
Twelve dollars per seat, quoted from the sheet's own row. If a quote isn't in what it read, the answer is dropped.
Let me think, I saw it on the dashboard.
That number was on my screen last week. Spark reads a crop of the dashboard.
Also, the launch is Friday the seventh now, right? Marketing told me Friday.
Hm, I thought it was the Monday. Let me check.
When the plan changes, the radar shows what we agreed in the planning meeting, with the quote.
Unrelated, but I'm showing LokalBot to a journalist on Friday. Is the radar panel hidden when I share my screen?
Hm, good question.
Wonder reads code too. It searches the repository, opens the settings, and links the exact line on GitHub.
Perfect. Let's go with twenty percent off for annual plans.
Agreed, twenty percent. Talk tomorrow!
After the call, it's all on the board: what we promised, decided, asked, and changed.

Follow-through takes my commitment from there. Wonder reads the meeting, searches the earlier ones, writes Ana an email that lays out the choice, and books our talk for tomorrow. Nothing is sent until I approve it.
Three Meta models, each where it fits: realtime speech, fast reading of text and images, and careful lookups and plans. Search and speaker separation stay on my Mac.
LokalBot. From meeting to done.
